content: Are all 50 validators fixed? If so, players with access to the contribution view might be able to inspect the groups used in the validators and potentially devise a hardcoded strategy for those specific instances.
Validators are fully random. Only the IDE test cases are fixed.
All right! Thank you for the quick response. I'll review the contribution as soon as I can.
Your feedback is always really helpful, appreciate any thoughts when you get a chance!

Thank you for your kind words 😊

I've just had a chance to review your contribution, and I noted the following points/suggestions:

The Goal
* Consider changing "hide" to "are divided into".

* Please add "in the fewest number of turns" as part of the goal.

Rules
* Please format 1, 16, 140, 10, "GREEN", "ORANGE" and "GREY" using the <const> tag.

The board
* "slide up": Do you mean "move down"?

Score
* I suggest using "score" consistently instead of introducing the separate term "points" and having two terms for the same quantity.

* Accordingly, you could change "descending order of the points received" to "players in descending order of their score", and also use "Score" instead of "Points" in the two formulas.

* "turnsUsed" is not defined elsewhere. Please change it to "number of turns used".

Defeat Conditions
* Please change "is not four distinct integers on one line" to "does not contain four distinct integers".

* Please rewrite the third condition as:
You make a guess containing a box number which is either outside the range 1 to 16, or from a group already solved.

Game Input
* Please remove "again".

* feedback: Consider listing "GREY", "ORANGE" and "GREEN" in the same order as in the "The hint" section for consistency.

Constraints
* Boxes are numbered 1 to 16: This duplicates information already given earlier, so I suggest removing it.

* "[[solvedGroups]] never reaches 4 (0 to 3)": Please clarify its meaning. You could choose one of the following:

  • [[solvedGroups]] is from <const>0</const> to <const>3</const> on the first turn, i.e. the game is never started with all four groups already solved.

  • 0 ≤ [[solvedGroups]] ≤ 3
  (But choose this only if the first option doesn't apply.)

  • (some other meaning?)

* Please add:
All tests are fixed, while all validators are random.

Stub
* Please change:
loop 4 read a:int b:int c:int d:int
to:
loop 4 loopline 4 box:int

Console
* It'll be useful if the score is shown at the end of the game (e.g. add a message "Score: 117").

* So far I've seen three kinds of end-game console messages:

(A)
Invalid guess: 3 9 6 8 13
Ended: invalid_output - 1/4 groups in 6 turns

(B)
Turn cap reached - 2/4 groups found.
Ended: turn_cap - 2/4 groups in 100 turns.

(C)
All four groups found in 8 turns.
Ended: solved - 4/4 groups in 8 turns.

The "invalid_output", "turn_cap" and "solved" labels don't appear to add useful information, since the preceding messages already explain why the game ended. In addition, the first two labels contain an underscore, which appears odd in a message. I suggest removing those labels.

I would also use "1 (or 2, 3 or 4) out of 4" instead of "1/4", "2/4", etc.

Suggested revised messages:

(A)
Invalid guess: 3 9 6 8 13
Game ended after ___ turns with ___ out of 4 groups found.
Score: ___

(B)
Turn cap reached.
Game ended after ___ turns with ___ out of 4 groups found.
Score: ___

(C)
Victory!
Game ended after ___ turns with ___ out of 4 groups found.
Score: ___

Thanks.

Thanks, this was really helpful. All applied.

On "slide up": you're right that it's wrong, though "move down" isn't quite right either. The newly solved row pushes the live boxes down, but they also close the gap left by the solved group, so some move each way. I've dropped the direction: "The boxes still in play close the gaps left behind, staying in ascending order." That sentence had a second mistake, which your question made me spot: a solved group lands below the ones already solved, not at the top. Fixed as well.

For solvedGroups, I went with 0 ≤ solvedGroups ≤ 3. It's not just the first turn. The game ends as soon as the fourth group is found, so the solver never sees a board with four solved rows.

Score is now "Score" consistently, in the statement and everywhere else it appears.

Your note on consistency also made me spot another one: the statement called it "the hint" in the rules but named the input feedback. I've renamed the input to hint in the stub and the statement.

On the console, there's a fourth ending you wouldn't have run into, a timeout, which now gets the same two lines as the others.

I also tagged the 100 in the victory and defeat conditions.

Thanks again!

Thank you for the update and explanations. They all make sense and are thoughtful as well. Well done!

I noted two remaining points:

Score
* "The leaderboard ranks players in descending order of their score." I'm unable to verify that this has been configured correctly, so please ensure that the configuration is correct. (There was an optimisation game previously where the leaderboard configuration was the opposite of what was intended and wasn't corrected until after approval.)

Viewer
* I didn't notice that the box numbers are displayed at the top left of each solved box. Please consider increasing their font size, perhaps to about 1/9 of the box area, so that they're more readily visible.

Thanks again.

Thanks, glad those made sense.

On the score configuration: I've built an optimization game(Wordle) before, which ranks players in ascending order of the guesses they made. This one is in descending order of score and I've configured it accordingly, so hopefully it will work correctly.

On the box numbers: you're right that they were too easy to miss, so I've made them noticeably bigger, from 22px to 32px on a 170px tile. I didn't go as far as a ninth of the box area though, because once a group is solved the colour and the item are meant to be the main content of the tile, with the number secondary to them. Their ink is already tuned per group against each tile colour so they stay readable on all four, and for anyone who wants numbers throughout, the viewer has a DEBUG option in the gear menu that shows every box as a number.

Thanks again!

Ah, that explains why your name looked familiar. I can definitely associate Tanvir with Wordle in my memory! 🙂

And the box numbers are big enough to be noticeable now, so that's good. Thanks for the explanation.

Ha, nice to be remembered for it! 🙂 Your feedback on Wordle was really helpful during that review too.

One thing I've noticed is that until a few groups are solved, the board stays quite plain, and the statement reads as just the rules. I'm planning to work on how the board looks and to give the statement a bit more character. I hope you'll take a look once those changes are in, and if you have any thoughts in the meantime, I'd be glad to hear them.

Thanks again for the review.
